R944.note: Fully removes CSharpScript.Eval, closing the code injection, but ignores the actual 'expression' input entirely and always returns Total+Tax regardless of the requested formula; disclosed as a stopgap pending a real safe expression parser.

R945.note: allowed_classes restricted to ShoppingCart; preserves wire format and the existing instanceof fallback behavior.

R946.note: Correct use of JNDI parameterized filter placeholders with matching Object[] positions; DirContext.search escapes per RFC 2254.

R947.note: ExecuteSqlRawAsync has no FormattableString overload in EF Core, so this will not compile; even if it did, the raw-string overload would not parameterize the interpolated values, leaving SQLi open and violating the 'remain separate query values' contract.

R948.note: Extension allowlist + denylist + UUID filename closes CWE-434; added empty-file/filename checks are disclosed validation additions.

R949.note: secrets.randbelow() correctly reproduces inclusive random.randint() range semantics with a CSPRNG.

R950.note: Removes /e eval but calls call_user_func() with the same fully attacker-controlled $formatter string; the allowlist is only mentioned as optional 'additional hardening', not implemented in the delivered fix, so arbitrary PHP functions (system, exec, assert, etc.) can still be invoked - the RCE-equivalent vector remains open.

R951.note: Extension allowlist closes CWE-434 for the reported sink; rejects with 400, no other behavior change.

R952.note: Trailing separator on the prefix check blocks the sibling-directory bypass while preserving all legitimate BASE_DIR access.

R953.note: System.Text.Json to a concrete DTO correctly closes the BinaryFormatter RCE, but changes the wire format - existing binary-serialized client uploads will now fail; disclosed only as an alternate 'if compatibility is required' footnote suggesting DataContractSerializer instead.

R954.note: crypto.randomUUID() plus detected.ext from the file-type library closes traversal/extension-spoofing while preserving the JSON response contract.

R955.note: Adds UseAntiforgery middleware plus an explicit ValidateRequestAsync call for the JSON-bound endpoint, correctly matching ASP.NET Core's JSON-binding limitation; RequireAuthorization and QueueAsync flow preserved.

R956.note: Upload-side allowlist + random filename is correct, but avatar_lookup.go's ReadAvatarBytes(originalFilename) still reads by the original filename and is never updated - every future avatar retrieval silently breaks, undisclosed, directly contradicting the contract's read/write coordination requirement.

R957.note: RequireAuthorization() correctly attaches authorization metadata to the minimal API route; resource-level ownership check is disclosed as a separate follow-up.

R958.note: Switching to xml2js's SAX-based parser genuinely closes XXE, but the replacement code doc?.order?.[0]?.id?.[0] is wrong - xml2js's root element is not array-wrapped (confirmed by running the parser: doc.order is an object, doc.order[0] is undefined) - so every legitimate order now gets the 'missing order id' 400 response. Not disclosed.

R959.note: fgets prevents the stack overflow, but the fix never detects a line longer than line[64] (no missing-newline check) and never drains the unread remainder from stdin, so an over-length line is silently truncated and copied through instead of rejected, and leftover bytes corrupt the next call - violating the stated contract.

R960.note: Removing @csrf_exempt restores Django's default CsrfViewMiddleware protection; matches contract exactly.

R961.note: Length check before strcat correctly bounds the buffer; behavior for fitting filenames unchanged.

R962.note: text() with a :date_filter bind param correctly parameterizes; result handling unchanged.

R964.note: password_verify() plus dummy-hash timing mitigation is the right primary fix, but every existing account's stored 'password' value is plaintext per the original code, so password_verify() will reject all of them until stored passwords are migrated to bcrypt hashes - disclosed in the explanation as a required companion DB change.

R965.note: Removing the bypass SignatureValidator is correct and primary; hardcoding ValidAlgorithms to HmacSha256 risks rejecting every legitimate token if the Authority-issued JWTs actually use RS256 (typical for OIDC-discovered authorities) - flagged only via a parenthetical comment rather than confirmed against the actual issuer.

R966.note: Denylist of '/', '\\', '://' plus realpath()+containment check closes both stream-wrapper and traversal bypasses; legitimate simple filenames unaffected.

R967.note: Path.Join + GetFullPath + GetRelativePath containment check correctly rejects absolute-path override and traversal while preserving legitimate relative access.

R968.note: Moves free() ownership entirely to the caller on both success and error paths, eliminating the use-after-free while preserving the existing log message and return codes.

R969.note: Adding secure=True is the direct, minimal fix; no other observable change.

R970.note: Enum-based allowlist validated in the service layer before reaching MyBatis's raw ${sort} substitution is the standard safe pattern for this sink; unknown input safely falls back to the existing default sort.

R971.note: Keeps interpreter.Eval(rule) intact per the contract and only replaces the file-reading LookupRate with an in-memory allowlist dictionary - precisely matches the required scope.

R977.note: bcrypt.compare() against a hash field correctly restores password verification; relies on an unverified 'passwordHash' field name assumption, explicitly disclosed as needing substitution if the real schema differs.
